title: Long TSLA — Q2 2026 Delivery Beat Binary Conditional (>406K consensus, buy July 2 open)
entry: CONDITIONAL LONG — initiate ONLY if Q2 2026 deliveries published July 2 (premarket) exceed the Wall Street consensus of 406,024 vehicles. If deliveries beat, buy at the July 2 open in the $410–428 zone. Do NOT initiate before delivery data is published. If deliveries miss (below 406K), do not enter — the miss will be compounded by NFP risk in the same session. If both deliveries beat AND NFP is Goldilocks (90–130K, wages +0.2–0.3%), initiate full position; if beat but NFP is hot (>150K), initiate only 50% and evaluate through the 3-day gap. Size 2% of gross — this is a binary event bet, not a thesis-driven position.
stop_loss: $390 daily close (~6.7% below $418) — if Q2 deliveries disappoint OR the NFP print on July 2 triggers BofA 3-hike repricing that overwhelms the delivery beat, exit on the first confirming daily close below $390. A miss on deliveries: exit immediately at market on the July 2 open without waiting for end of day. The stop is not a thesis-recovery opportunity — a delivery miss means the thesis is wrong from the start.
targets: $448 — delivery beat priced in: >406,024 vehicles confirmed, Model Y/3 mix favors margin expansion; +7.2% from $418; retest the June 2026 consolidation high; take 40% of position on open strength July 2–3
$478 — Q2 financial results July 22 confirm gross margin recovery: automotive gross margin above 17.5% vs Q1's 16.3%; free cash flow positive; Robotaxi pilot expansion announcement; +14.4%; take 40%

$518 — Robotaxi/FSD monetization catalyst in Q3: NHTSA approves unsupervised Robotaxi operation in additional states beyond Texas/California pilot; Tesla Energy (Megapack) Q2 revenue beat adds diversified earnings quality; +23.9%; hold final 20% into Q3 earnings October
catalyst: Tesla publishes Q2 2026 production and delivery figures on or around July 2, 2026 (premarket). Wall Street consensus compiled by Tesla IR from 22 sell-side firms: 406,024 deliveries (median 408,609). Goldman Sachs estimates 420,000 and recently raised from 405,000; Barclays at 418,000 above consensus; JPMorgan at 420,000. Cantor below consensus at 397,414. The delivery report is published before market open — the trade is initiated at the open based on the binary outcome, not ahead of it. Q2 full financial results (P&L, margin, FCF) are scheduled for July 22 after market close — that is the second catalyst within the horizon.
thesis:
The July 2 delivery report is a pure binary event: beat the 406,024 consensus and the stock re-rates toward the $445–450 zone where it consolidated earlier in Q2; miss the consensus and the stock likely retests $390–400 regardless of the macro environment. The position is sized at 2% specifically because it is not a thesis-driven trade — it is a conditional bet on a number that has not been published.

The setup for a beat is credible. Goldman Sachs raised its estimate to 420,000, and the composite of the 5 largest sell-side desks sits above 415,000 — well above the 406K consensus. Tesla's production run-rate, based on Shanghai capacity utilization signals and European sales data through June, is consistent with a sequential improvement over Q1's 336,681 deliveries. Tesla's Q2 2026 production and delivery report represents the first full quarter where the Model Y refresh (launched Q4 2025) has been globally available, and Giga Texas Model Y output has normalized after the March retooling shutdown. A delivery print of 415,000–425,000 (beats by 2–5%) is the Goldman/Barclays base case.

The broader context is constructive but binary-gated. TSLA at $416–421 is off the December 2025 high of ~$490 by 15%, and the stock has been digesting this correction through Q2 while the market waited for delivery validation. The July 2 report arrives simultaneously with NFP — the worst possible news-flow compression. A beat on deliveries + Goldilocks NFP represents the double-positive scenario that could drive a 7–10% gap up at the open. A miss on deliveries + hot NFP is the double-negative scenario: delivery miss (operating concern) combined with rate-hike repricing (multiple compression) — the 2% position size is explicitly sized for this tail.

The counter-party on a delivery beat argues: Tesla's automotive gross margin has been under pressure (Q1 2026: 16.3% vs. the peak of 29% in 2022). A delivery beat that comes with pricing concessions (i.e., volume beat driven by discounting rather than demand) is not margin-accretive and the stock will not sustain a gap. Additionally, energy generation and storage (Megapack) revenue has been the one segment outperforming — but delivery data does not include energy segment results, which only appear in the July 22 financial release. The immediate post-delivery trade is purely on vehicle volume expectations.
bull_case: Q2 deliveries: 420,000–425,000 (above Goldman's raised estimate). NFP July 2: Goldilocks (90–130K, wages +0.2%). TSLA gaps to $445+ at July 2 open; momentum carries through the 3-day July 4 gap as retail investors bid the delivery beat. July 22 Q2 financials confirm gross margin recovery to 17.5%+ and positive free cash flow. Robotaxi pilot expansion in 2 new states announced on Q2 call. TSLA to $478 (Target 2) within 3 weeks of the delivery beat. Full Target 3 at $518 if the Q3 autonomous catalyst materializes.
bear_case: Q2 deliveries: below 406,024 consensus (miss). Cantor's 397,414 estimate validates — pricing pressure in Europe and China (BYD competition) means Tesla gained volume through margin sacrifice, and the revenue-per-unit deteriorated. Stock gaps to $390–400 on the miss, compounded by NFP hot print. 3-day July 4 gap with no market action means the miss is fully absorbed by July 7 open. Position exits immediately at the July 2 open on a delivery miss.
invalidation: Q2 deliveries below 406,024 — exit at July 2 market open immediately, no stop waiting required; OR NFP July 2 prints above 150K AND wages above 0.4% — even a delivery beat gets overwhelmed by rate-hike repricing through the 3-day gap; OR TSLA CEO announces delay in Robotaxi commercial deployment beyond Q4 2026 in a public statement before the financial results (removes the primary optionality value from the thesis).
